findings.evidence: Lines 95, 99-100 show the hand-instantiated `ite_eq_*` chain. Changing the if-condition orientation in either upstream coefficient lemma would break every term in it.
findings.fix: Pass the case hypotheses to `simp`, e.g. `simp [hn, hprev, hn.le, hn.ne', not_le.mpr hn]`, or replace the branches with `split_ifs <;> first | omega | simp`.
findings.issue: `circleFourierIndexOperator_fourierCoeff` closes each trichotomy branch with a `simp only` list of if-then-else terms built by hand (`ite_eq_right (not_le.mpr hprev)`, `ite_eq_left hn.le`, `ite_eq_right (not_lt.mpr hn.le)`, `ite_eq_right hn.ne'`, ...; lines 95-100). This ties the proof to the exact condition form (`0 ≤ n` vs `n < 0`, negated or not) produced by `fourierCoeff_fourierLp_smul` and `fourierCoeff_hardySubmodule_starProjection`.

findings.evidence: Lines 114-118: `simpa only [circleFourierIndexOperator_fourierCoeff, ite_eq_left hn]` and `ite_eq_right hn₁, ite_eq_right hn₂, add_sub_cancel_right`.
findings.fix: Use `simpa [circleFourierIndexOperator_fourierCoeff, hn] using hcoeff n`. In the second branch, use `simpa [circleFourierIndexOperator_fourierCoeff, show ¬n + 1 < 0 by omega, show n + 1 ≠ 0 by omega] using hcoeff (n + 1)`, or state a recovery lemma `fourierCoeff (A f) (n+1) = fourierCoeff f n` for `0 ≤ n`.
findings.issue: `ker_circleFourierIndexOperator` repeats the same pattern: both `simpa only` calls (lines 114 and 117) resolve the if-then-else from `circleFourierIndexOperator_fourierCoeff` with hand-picked `ite_eq_left hn`, `ite_eq_right hn₁`, `ite_eq_right hn₂`, and the helper hypotheses `hn₁`/`hn₂` exist only to feed them.

summary: Two coefficient case splits are closed by long chains of hand-instantiated `ite_eq_left`/`ite_eq_right` terms, which break if the if-then-else form of the coefficient lemmas changes; the rest of the proofs are short and robust.
